```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = FALSE, warning = FALSE, message = FALSE)

# Helpers identicos a report/incident_report_template.rmd (mesma convencao
# visual em todos os relatorios do projeto)
report_table <- function(x, max_col_width_cm = NULL) {
  ft <- flextable::flextable(round_display(x)) |>
    flextable::theme_box() |>
    flextable::bg(part = "header", bg = "gray85") |>
    flextable::bold(part = "header") |>
    flextable::fontsize(size = 9, part = "header") |>
    flextable::fontsize(size = 9, part = "body") |>
    flextable::align(align = "center", part = "header") |>
    flextable::valign(valign = "center", part = "all") |>
    flextable::autofit()
  if (!is.null(max_col_width_cm)) ft <- cap_col_width(ft, max_col_width_cm)
  ft
}

round_display <- function(x, digits = 2) {
  x <- as.data.frame(x)
  for (col in names(x)) {
    v <- x[[col]]
    if (!is.numeric(v) || is.integer(v)) next
    if (all(v == round(v), na.rm = TRUE)) next
    x[[col]] <- vapply(v, function(val) {
      if (is.na(val)) return(NA_character_)
      d <- digits
      while (round(val, d) == 0 && val != 0 && d < 6) d <- d + 1
      sprintf(paste0("%.", d, "f"), val)
    }, character(1))
  }
  x
}

cap_col_width <- function(ft, max_width_cm = 2) {
  widths_in <- dim(ft)$widths
  capped_cm <- pmin(widths_in * 2.54, max_width_cm)
  flextable::width(ft, j = seq_along(capped_cm), width = capped_cm, unit = "cm")
}

rename_display <- function(x, mapping) {
  x <- as.data.frame(x)
  idx <- match(names(mapping), names(x))
  hit <- !is.na(idx)
  names(x)[idx[hit]] <- unname(mapping)[hit]
  x
}

# Um paragrafo em branco entre blocos texto/tabela/figura (mesma regra do
# relatorio de incidente: nunca 2 paragrafos em branco seguidos)
gap <- function() cat("\n\n&nbsp;\n\n")

heading <- function(level, txt) cat("\n\n", strrep("#", level), " ", txt, "\n\n", sep = "")

# Figura: guarda o ggplot num PNG temporario com a altura certa e inclui-o
# (caminho absoluto)
show_plot <- function(fig) {
  if (is.null(fig) || is.null(fig$p)) {
    cat("No data available for this figure.\n\n")
    return(invisible(NULL))
  }
  f <- tempfile(fileext = ".png")
  ggplot2::ggsave(f, fig$p, width = 6.3, height = fig$h, dpi = 150)
  # markdown direto (caminho absoluto): cat(knit_print(include_graphics())) so'
  # imprimia o caminho como texto
  cat(sprintf("\n\n![](%s)\n\n", normalizePath(f, winslash = "/")))
  invisible(NULL)
}

show_table <- function(df, max_col_width_cm = 2.4) {
  if (is.null(df) || nrow(df) == 0L) {
    cat("No data available for this table.\n\n")
    return(invisible(NULL))
  }
  cat(knitr::knit_print(report_table(df, max_col_width_cm = max_col_width_cm)))
  invisible(NULL)
}

annex_note <- function(xlsx_name) {
  if (!is.null(xlsx_name) && nzchar(xlsx_name)) {
    cat(sprintf("\n\n&nbsp;\n\n*The full tables are available in the accompanying workbook: `%s`.*\n", xlsx_name))
  }
}

# Uma epoca (outono/primavera): series sazonais, timing, correlacao por lag e
# seguimento dos pulsos
season_block <- function(key) {
  heading(1, params$season_titles[[key]])
  cat(sprintf(
    "Leader -> follower pairs: %s. A positive lag or lead means the follower farm shows the same pattern later than the leader farm, that is, the leader anticipates the follower.\n",
    params$season_pairs_text[[key]]
  ))

  heading(2, "Seasonal series")
  cat("Daily maximum of the minimum number of individuals in 2-minute bins (centred moving mean of ", params$smooth_days, " days), one panel per season and year, all farms on the same dates.\n", sep = "")
  for (sp in params$species) {
    gap()
    show_plot(params$plots$season_series[[key]][[sp]])
  }

  heading(2, "Timing of passage")
  cat("Onset, median and end of the passage are the first days on which the cumulative share of the season's daily maxima reaches ",
      params$onset_share * 100, "%, ", params$median_share * 100, "% and ", params$end_share * 100, "%. Lead is the follower date minus the leader date, in days. Seasons with insufficient monitoring are marked.\n", sep = "")
  gap()
  show_table(params$tables$timing[[key]])

  heading(2, "Lagged correlation")
  cat("Correlation between the leader's daily series at day t and the follower's at day t + lag, for lags from -", params$max_lag_days, " to +", params$max_lag_days, " days.\n", sep = "")
  for (sp in params$species) {
    gap()
    show_plot(params$plots$ccf[[key]][[sp]])
  }
  gap()
  show_table(params$tables$ccf[[key]])

  heading(2, "Pulse follow-up")
  cat("A pulse is a run of days with a daily maximum of at least ", params$pulse_min_individuals,
      " individual(s), merging runs separated by up to ", params$pulse_merge_gap_days,
      " days. For each leader pulse, the table gives how many were followed by a follower pulse starting within the next ",
      params$pulse_window_days, " days, the median lag, and the share of leader pulses with a follower pulse already present in the ",
      params$pulse_window_days, " days before (control).\n", sep = "")
  gap()
  show_table(params$tables$pulses[[key]])
}
```

**Regional Assessment** -- `r params$farms_text`

Species: **`r params$species_text`** | Analysis window: `r params$window_start` to `r params$window_end`

Analysis date: `r params$analysis_date` | Responsible Team: `r params$username` | Code version: `r params$code_version`

This report is descriptive and fully automated, generated end-to-end by an R code pipeline. It compares the weekly pattern of the two species in the three farms and the timing of their autumn and spring movements between farms.

---

# Data and methods

## Data coverage

Track records of the three farms in the analysis window, after removing duplicated records. A day is monitored when at least `r params$min_tracks_per_day` distinct tracks of any species were recorded.

&nbsp;

```{r data-coverage, results='asis'}
show_table(rename_display(params$data_coverage, c(
  farm = "Farm", first_day = "First day", last_day = "Last day",
  n_days_monitored = "Monitored days", n_track_rows = "Track records"
)))
```

## Weekly maximum

Track points of each species are grouped in time bins of `r params$bin_min` minutes. Within a bin, two tracks count as one individual when the minimum distance between any of their points is below `r params$merge_dist_m` m, so the number of individuals per bin is a minimum. The daily maximum is the highest value of the day, and the weekly maximum the highest daily maximum of each calendar week (Monday to Sunday), with the same weeks in the three farms. Days without monitoring have no value, and weeks with fewer than `r params$min_monitored_days` monitored days have no weekly value.

## Anticipation metrics

Seasons: `r params$seasons_text`. Three metrics are computed for each season, year, species and leader -> follower pair:

- **Timing of passage**: onset, median and end of the passage, from the cumulative daily maxima. A season has a timing only when monitored days cover at least `r params$min_season_coverage * 100`% of the season and the season total is at least `r params$min_season_total`.
- **Lagged correlation**: correlation between the daily series of the two farms for lags up to `r params$max_lag_days` days, after a centred moving mean of `r params$smooth_days` days, with at least `r params$min_overlap_days` overlapping days.
- **Pulse follow-up**: whether a pulse of the leader farm is followed by a pulse of the follower farm within `r params$pulse_window_days` days.

# Annual pattern

Weekly maximum of the minimum number of individuals in the three farms, for each species.

```{r annual-pattern, results='asis'}
for (sp in params$species) {
  heading(2, sp)
  cat("Weekly maximum by farm over the analysis window, and the same values by ISO week of the year, one line per farm and year.\n")
  gap()
  show_plot(params$plots$weekly[[sp]])
  gap()
  show_plot(params$plots$annual[[sp]])
  gap()
  show_table(rename_display(
    params$weekly_peak[params$weekly_peak$spec == sp, setdiff(names(params$weekly_peak), "spec"), drop = FALSE],
    c(farm = "Farm", peak_weekly_max = "Peak weekly maximum", peak_week_start = "Week of peak (Monday)",
      weeks_with_data = "Weeks with data", weeks_present = "Weeks with the species")
  ))
}
```

```{r season-autumn, results='asis'}
season_block("autumn")
```

```{r season-spring, results='asis'}
season_block("spring")
```

# Annexes

```{r annexes, results='asis'}
cat("Parameters used in this analysis.\n")
gap()
show_table(rename_display(params$parameters, c(Parameter = "Parameter", Value = "Value")), max_col_width_cm = 8)
annex_note(params$xlsx_name)
if (!is.null(params$extra_png_files) && length(params$extra_png_files) > 0L) {
  cat("\n\nFigures not shown in the report body, saved as image files in the same output folder:\n\n")
  cat(paste0("- `", params$extra_png_files, "`", collapse = "\n"), "\n", sep = "")
}
```
